mil3.2.2:1.2: “Venerable Nāgasena, does one who is not reborn know: ‘I will not be reborn’?”
mil3.2.2:1.3: “Yes, Great King, one who is not reborn knows: ‘I will not be reborn’.”
mil3.2.2:1.5: “Great King, with the ending of whatever cause and whatever condition there is for rebirth, he knows: ‘I will not be reborn’.”
mil3.2.2:2.2: “Suppose, Great King, a householder farmer were to plow and sow and fill his granary.
mil3.2.2:2.3: After some time he would neither plow nor sow, and would consume the grain he had stored up, or give it away, or do with it whatever was needed. Great King, would that householder farmer know: ‘My granary will not be filled’?”
mil3.2.2:2.6: “With the ending of whatever cause and whatever condition there is for filling the granary, he knows: ‘My granary will not be filled’.”
mil3.2.2:2.7: “In the same way, Great King, with the ending of whatever cause and whatever condition there is for rebirth, he knows: ‘I will not be reborn’.”
